meanings.note: Borrowed via German 'Pastete' from Old French/Italian 'pâté'/'pastetto', referring to finely ground seasoned meat or liver.

examples.trans: The chef prepares a signature pâté.
Chef, this is simply amazing pâté!

examples.text: Костя, быстро попробуй мой новый паштет.
examples.trans: Kostya, quickly taste my new pâté.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beef').

examples.text: Приготовь нежный говяжий паштет для гостей.
examples.trans: Prepare a tender beef pate for the guests.

examples.text: На плите уже три часа варится крепкий говяжий бульон.
examples.trans: A rich beef broth has been simmering on the stove for three hours.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'disgusting thing'.

examples.trans: He says nasty things about me.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'terrible' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('nothing serious') ('ничего страшного') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Теперь мы одна команда.
examples.trans: Nothing serious. Now we're one team.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мешать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'mix, blend'.

examples.trans: But when you mix it all together...

examples.text: Сначала нужно осторожно смешать сливки с тёплым шоколадом.
examples.trans: First you need to carefully blend the cream with warm chocolate.

examples.text: Если смешать эти два соуса, получится совершенно новый вкус.
examples.trans: If you mix these two sauces, you will get a completely new flavor.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: the person who likes is in the dative: мне нравится = I like it

examples.trans: The reaction is positive. People like it.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

издеваться.gloss: to mock, to kid, to mess with

meanings.en: to mock, to tease; colloquially 'are you kidding me?'
meanings.note: Ты что, издеваешься? = Are you kidding me?
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'why'.

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'амовоспитываться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'educate oneself'.

examples.trans: You were learning to discipline yourself.

examples.text: Всю эту неделю на кухне ты упорно самовоспитывался.
examples.trans: All this week in the kitchen you were persistently disciplining yourself.

examples.text: Настоящий мастер должен уметь каждый день самовоспитываться в труде.
examples.trans: A true master must know how to discipline himself in his work every day.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('oh come on!') (ну, папа!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'идти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.en: by the way, speaking of which
meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'by the way'.
Secondary conversational sense ('handy, well-timed') (это очень кстати) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh, by the way, I almost forgot.

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.
Secondary conversational sense ('as') (как вы знаете = as you know) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to make') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: to add, supplement, put in as an addition
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'бавлять'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to add'.

examples.text: Я добавляю свежую зелень и соус.
examples.trans: I add fresh greens and sauce.

examples.text: Макс, быстрее! Уже пора добавлять яйца.
examples.trans: Max, faster! It is time to add the eggs.
Add the dye slowly and carefully.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'beef' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Для этого блюда нам нужна свежая говядина.
examples.trans: We need fresh beef for this dish.

examples.text: Шеф заказал лучшую мраморную говядину для стейков.
examples.trans: The chef ordered the finest marbled beef for the steaks.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'liver', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Он умер здесь от болезни печени.
examples.trans: He died right here of liver disease.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'until' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('goodbye') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'meeting' in conversational and formal Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('date (romantic)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
